title: POS & Inventory Management
description: Archive Room — production consignment POS on Vercel + Neon. Tablet checkout, multi-tenant shops, inventory, and reporting; actively developed and supported for real shop-floor use.

caseStudy.role: Solo product engineer owning UI architecture, auth, inventory domain, and reporting for a consigned clothing POS — still shipping releases after go-live.
caseStudy.challenge: Shop staff needed fast tablet checkout and reliable stock/consignment tracking without a heavyweight ERP, then ongoing support once the pilot went live.
approach: Designed checkout and inventory screens for touch-first tablet use.
Modeled consignment and stock states with typed Prisma schemas.
Shipped multi-tenant shops, offline POS, and platform ops while keeping production stable.
architecture: Next.js App Router with role-aware API routes and JWT sessions.
PostgreSQL via Prisma on Neon for durable inventory and sales history.
Vercel deploy with Blob uploads, PWA offline queue, and contract automation.
quality: Smoke tests and CI around login, POS sale, and day close.
Defensive UI for stale stock, suspended shops, and concurrent edits.
Ops docs for pilot onboard, backups, and release gates.
caseStudy.outcome: A live POS (Archive Room) in continuous development — not a parked demo — prioritizing tablet speed and trustworthy consignment inventory.

title: Frontend Design System Migration
description: Token-driven Next.js workspace with reusable primitives, a live playground, and Storybook + Vitest gates — so apps migrate off one-off UI drift.

caseStudy.role: Frontend platform owner defining tokens, primitives, and adoption paths for consuming apps.
caseStudy.challenge: Product UIs drifted into one-off styles with weak shared contracts and little regression safety.
approach: Established semantic tokens mapped to host themes.
Built forms, feedback, and overlay primitives with documented APIs.
Wired Storybook and Vitest into CI so visual contracts stay enforceable.
architecture: Next.js workspace separating tokens, primitives, and playground.
Tailwind + CSS custom properties for theme remapping.
Storybook as the living catalog for migration teams.
quality: Component tests for interaction-critical primitives.
CI gates before consumers adopt new versions.
Clear migration guidance to reduce copy-paste UI.
caseStudy.outcome: A reusable system that makes consistent UI the default path, not the exception.

title: FLASHCUT
description: Real-time party game: peek an image, survive the flashcut blackout, then race Kahoot-style scoring across 15 rounds — Next.js, Redis rooms, and Vercel-friendly polling.

caseStudy.role: Full product owner for realtime game UX, room state, and serverless-friendly sync.
caseStudy.challenge: Need multiplayer round timing that works on Vercel serverless without sticky WebSocket hosts.
approach: Modeled host/player rooms with Redis-backed state.
Used HTTP polling tuned for serverless constraints.
Shipped host-editable image packs for replayable sessions.
architecture: Next.js routes for lobby, round phases, and scoring.
Upstash Redis for ephemeral room state across instances.
Polling contract designed for reconnects mid-round.
quality: Vitest coverage for scoring and phase transitions.
Graceful handling when players drop mid-round.
UX that stays readable under time pressure.
caseStudy.outcome: A playable realtime game that stays deployable on serverless infrastructure.

title: Realtime Operations Dashboard
description: WebSocket-driven ops board with health tiles, alerts, and reconnect/stale-data UX — plus a self-contained event simulator for demos.

caseStudy.role: Frontend architect for realtime visualization, connection resilience, and demo simulation.
caseStudy.challenge: Ops dashboards often hide stale data and break silently when sockets disconnect.
approach: Surfaced service health and alert states as first-class UI.
Designed reconnect and stale-data affordances operators can trust.
Built an event simulator so the board is demoable without production traffic.
architecture: Next.js client surfaces fed by WebSocket event streams.
PostgreSQL + Redis backing for durable and ephemeral state.
Clear boundaries between live events and simulated feeds.
quality: Visible stale/reconnect states instead of silent failure.
Alert presentation tuned for scanning under pressure.
Demo mode that still exercises real client sync paths.
caseStudy.outcome: A realtime dashboard pattern that treats connection health as part of the product.

title: AI-Assisted Incident Triage
description: Ops triage console where Gemini suggests severity, ownership, and runbooks — with keyword fallback, confidence UX, human override, and a full audit trail. Portfolio demo on free-tier stack.

caseStudy.role: Full-stack owner for AI-assisted triage UX, suggestion pipeline, and safety/fallback behavior.
caseStudy.challenge: AI triage demos often auto-apply model output. Real ops need suggestions inside a workflow with override, confidence, and auditability when the model fails.
approach: Built intake → suggest → override → accept as one operator path.
Used Gemini for structured JSON triage with Zod validation against a seeded runbook catalog.
Added deterministic keyword rules when the key is missing, rate-limited, or invalid.
architecture: Next.js App Router APIs for incidents, suggest, and triage decisions.
PostgreSQL + Prisma for incidents, suggestions, runbooks, and audit events.
Server-only Gemini key with IP rate limits, daily budget, and per-incident caps.
quality: Vitest coverage for rule triage and guard helpers.
Sanitized client fallback copy (no raw provider quota leaks).
Confidence bar and low-confidence warning before accept.
caseStudy.outcome: A demo-ready triage console that treats AI as an assistant — humans still decide, and failures degrade to rules instead of breaking the flow.

title: Developer Productivity Portal
description: Internal ship desk: CI rollups, release notes, and service health with acknowledge/publish actions — fixture data plus optional GitHub Actions and Releases sync.

caseStudy.role: Full-stack owner for a platform-engineering portal: CI insights, release workflow, and service health with clear data-source boundaries.
caseStudy.challenge: Developer dashboards often stop at read-only status tiles. Teams need an actionable workflow and clear auth/data-boundary documentation without paid integrations.
approach: Shipped a Harbor Commerce fixture seed so the portal works without external credentials.
Unified CI runs and release notes in shared tables with fixture + optional GitHub adapters.
Made acknowledge failing checks, acknowledge degradation, and draft/publish release notes first-class actions with an activity trail.
architecture: Next.js App Router pages (RSC) with mutation APIs for acknowledge, publish, and sync.
PostgreSQL + Prisma for services, CI runs, releases, quick links, and activity events.
Server-only GitHub token; Zod-validated Actions/Releases payloads upserted by external id.
quality: Walkthrough documented: ack CI → draft/publish release → activity feed.
ARCHITECTURE.md covers adapters, tradeoffs, and v1 auth boundaries (no login).
Sync fails closed to fixture-only when token or repo list is missing.
caseStudy.outcome: A ship desk with two data sources and operator actions — CI, releases, and health in one workflow instead of a read-only dashboard.

title: Portfolio CMS + Publishing Workflow
description: Next.js CMS for portfolio content in PostgreSQL — draft preview, role-aware admin, and GitHub PR publishing so content updates stay auditable and reviewable.

caseStudy.role: Solo builder owning auth, document model, preview, and GitHub publish flow for a separate portfolio repo.
caseStudy.challenge: Portfolio content lived in the site repo with no safe draft/preview path — updates were either manual commits or risky direct edits.
approach: Modeled content documents with slug, JSON payload, and workflow status in Postgres.
Built ADMIN edit/publish and draft preview routes behind NextAuth.
Wired publish to open a PR against the portfolio repo with an auditable PublishRun history.
architecture: Next.js App Router with Zod-validated content APIs.
Prisma + PostgreSQL for documents and publish runs.
GitHub REST publish: branch → file updates → PR, with optional Redis rate limits.
quality: Vitest coverage around services and publish contracts.
Role gates so only ADMIN can publish.
Explicit publishing contract so CMS JSON maps cleanly to portfolio paths.
caseStudy.outcome: Faster content turnaround with preview and PR review instead of blind commits to the live site.

title: BOQ Digital Banking Platform
description: Senior frontend delivery for BOQ banking experiences under NRI ANZ — reusable UI patterns and release guardrails in regulated workflows.

caseStudy.role: Senior frontend engineer for architecture, implementation standards, and delivery quality across critical journeys.
caseStudy.challenge: Regulated banking delivery requires velocity without sacrificing reliability, security, or review depth.
approach: Standardized reusable UI patterns across squads.
Introduced release guardrails for risky UI changes.
Strengthened test strategy for key customer flows.
architecture: Feature-oriented frontend structure for ownership boundaries.
Typed contracts and shared utilities for consistency.
Progressive rollout patterns for high-risk changes.
quality: Automated coverage for critical user paths.
PR checklists for reliability and accessibility.
Post-release validation for faster issue detection.
caseStudy.outcome: Improved release confidence while keeping delivery sustainable in regulated workflows.

title: Helika Analytics Platform
description: Frontend architecture for a data-heavy analytics product — dashboard performance, shared patterns, and team delivery standards.

caseStudy.role: Senior frontend owner for architecture and performance of analytics surfaces.
caseStudy.challenge: Large datasets and inconsistent patterns slowed rendering and delivery.
approach: Optimized rendering paths for expensive dashboard components.
Created reusable dashboard patterns and state conventions.
Embedded quality standards into reviews and workflows.
architecture: Modular React + TypeScript dashboard composition.
Predictable state with Redux Toolkit.
Shared visualization primitives for consistency.
quality: Performance budgets on primary dashboard pages.
Component-level tests for critical interactions.
Structured reviews to prevent pattern drift.
caseStudy.outcome: Faster dashboards and more reliable releases for a data-heavy product.
